scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. We've been living together for two years, and we moved to our current apartment a year ago. The main reason we moved was because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy without roommates. That worked out well until recently when J ended up moving back in with us. From what I gather, J had some issues with her previous roommates. She didn't pay rent for two months, which caused some financial strain. The landlords were accepting cash, so it's unclear if they were aware of the situation. J managed to get the money from her family to pay off the rent and then asked my girlfriend, L, and me to let her stay with us until the end of January. She mentioned that her uncle would pick her up and she'd move out of state, but it seems like she's not really planning to go through with that. Instead, she's been staying in New York, partying every other night, and using our place as a hangover den. My girlfriend isn't confrontational, so she hasn't opposed J living with us for free. However, J doesn't have a job, only occasionally contributes by cooking, and spends most of her time partying. This is affecting our home life, and I'm really conflicted because J is her sister. I don't want to upset L, but I also want my home back. I've tried getting L to talk to J about it, but she avoids confrontation. I'm considering telling J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her own place, she needs to move back to her mother's. I'm worried L will be mad at me, but I feel like it's necessary to take this step. Now, thinking about this from a Christian perspective, I need to consider the principles of love, respect, and responsibility. The Bible teaches us to love our neighbors as ourselves and to act justly. However, it also emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's household and providing for one's family. I should also consider the impact on all parties involved. Kicking J out might seem harsh, but if she's not contributing and is causing disruption, it might be necessary for the well-being of our relationship and our home. On the other hand, as L's sister, J might be going through a tough time, and helping her could be seen as a compassionate act. I'm also thinking about the practical aspects. Do we have the means to support J indefinitely? It doesn't seem sustainable, especially since J isn't looking for work despite the current situation. There's a responsibility to ensure that our living situation remains stable and comfortable for both L and me. Another angle is the concept of boundaries. Setting clear boundaries is important in any relationship, including with family. If J is not respecting our space and lifestyle, it might be necessary to set those boundaries, even if it means she has to leave. I'm also reflecting on how this decision aligns with my values. Do I value my home and peace more than avoiding conflict with L? It's a tough balance, but I think it's important to stand up for what's right for our relationship and our living situation. In conclusion, while it's difficult to consider kicking J out, especially since she's family, the circumstances seem to warrant it. It's about balancing compassion with practicality and maintaining a healthy living environment.
